subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which Christian tradition is marriage regarded as a sacrament?
options: Roman Catholicism
The Religious Society of Friends (Quakers)
The Salvation Army
Most Baptist churches
questions.explain: Roman Catholicism teaches that marriage is one of the seven sacraments, an outward sign of God's grace.

questions.q: What does 'monogamy' mean?
options: Being married to only one partner at a time
Being married to several partners at once
Choosing never to marry
Living together without marriage
questions.explain: Monogamy is marriage to one partner at a time and is the expected form of marriage in Christianity.

questions.q: Under Islamic law, a Muslim man may marry a maximum of how many wives, provided he treats them equally?
options: Four
One
Two
There is no limit
questions.explain: Islam permits a man up to four wives on the condition that he can treat them all fairly and equally.

questions.q: What is the name of the Islamic marriage contract?
options: Nikah
Mahr
Ummah
Halal
questions.explain: The nikah is the marriage contract in Islam, while the mahr is the gift given by the groom to the bride.

questions.q: Why do many Roman Catholics believe that marriage cannot be ended by divorce?
options: Because the marriage bond is a sacrament joined by God and is therefore lifelong
Because divorce is forbidden by the laws of every country
Because only priests are allowed to end a marriage
Because remarriage is impossible after a partner dies
questions.explain: Catholics hold that what God has joined in the sacrament of marriage is indissoluble, so it lasts for life.

questions.q: Which of these best describes a key religious purpose of the family?
options: To raise and nurture children within the faith
To increase a family's wealth and status
To ensure parents are cared for in old age only
To keep religious traditions completely private
questions.explain: Religions commonly teach that a central purpose of the family is to bring up children and pass on faith and values.

questions.q: A Roman Catholic woman wants her marriage declared never to have been valid so she can remarry in church. What is she seeking?
options: An annulment
A divorce
A separation
A remarriage vow
questions.explain: An annulment is a Church declaration that a valid marriage never existed, unlike a divorce which ends a valid marriage.

questions.q: A couple decide to live together and have a sexual relationship without marrying. How would many traditional religious believers most likely respond?
options: They would disapprove, teaching that sex belongs within marriage
They would fully approve as a modern form of marriage
They would insist the couple must never marry later
They would treat it as identical to a religious marriage
questions.explain: Many traditional believers teach that sexual relationships should take place only within marriage, so they discourage cohabitation.

questions.q: What does a 'complementarian' view of gender teach?
options: Men and women have different but complementary God-given roles
Men and women should have identical roles in every area
Only women should hold religious authority
Gender roles have no religious significance
questions.explain: Complementarianism holds that men and women are equal in worth but have different, complementary roles.

questions.q: A believer holds an 'egalitarian' view of gender. Which statement best reflects this?
options: Men and women should have equal roles and opportunities in religion and society
Only men should lead worship and the household
Women should not take paid employment
Men and women can never share domestic tasks
questions.explain: An egalitarian view teaches that men and women are equal and should share roles and opportunities equally.

questions.q: Why might some traditional believers support the man being the main breadwinner and the woman caring for the home?
options: They believe scripture and tradition assign distinct, complementary family roles
They believe women are less intelligent than men
They believe women are forbidden from all education
They believe men should never care for children
questions.explain: Traditional believers often appeal to scripture and tradition to support different but complementary roles for husband and wife.

questions.q: The verse 'there is neither male nor female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus' is often used to support which idea?
options: The spiritual equality of men and women
The superiority of men over women
The abolition of marriage
A ban on women attending church
questions.explain: This teaching from Galatians is used to argue that men and women are spiritually equal before God.

questions.q: A Christian denomination decides to ordain women as priests on the same basis as men. This best reflects which view of gender?
options: An egalitarian view
A complementarian view
A polygamous view
A celibate view
questions.explain: Ordaining women on equal terms reflects an egalitarian belief that men and women should have equal roles.

questions.q: What is 'adultery'?
options: Sexual relations between a married person and someone who is not their spouse
Marrying more than one partner at a time
Choosing never to marry or have sex
Sexual relations between two unmarried people
questions.explain: Adultery is voluntary sexual activity between a married person and someone other than their marriage partner.

questions.q: Which of the Ten Commandments most directly upholds faithfulness within marriage?
options: 'You shall not commit adultery'
'You shall not steal'
'You shall not bear false witness'
'Honour your father and your mother'
questions.explain: The commandment against adultery directly supports faithfulness between marriage partners.

questions.q: Official Roman Catholic teaching, as set out in Humanae Vitae, is that artificial contraception is:
options: Not permitted
Strongly encouraged
Required within marriage
A matter of no moral concern
questions.explain: Humanae Vitae (1968) taught that artificial contraception is wrong, though natural family planning is allowed.

questions.q: What does 'celibacy' mean?
options: Abstaining from marriage and sexual relations, often for religious reasons
Being married to one partner for life
Using contraception within marriage
Marrying more than one partner
questions.explain: Celibacy is the choice to abstain from marriage and sexual activity, as taken by Catholic priests, monks and nuns.

questions.q: Why do many Protestant Christians accept the use of contraception within marriage?
options: They believe responsible family planning can be a loving and caring decision
They believe children are unimportant to marriage
They believe marriage should have no sexual relationship
They believe the Bible commands the use of contraception
questions.explain: Many Protestants accept contraception as a responsible way for couples to plan a family and express love.

questions.q: Which statement best contrasts traditional and liberal religious views on homosexual relationships?
options: Traditional believers often teach sex belongs within heterosexual marriage, while liberal believers may accept loving same-sex relationships
Both traditional and liberal believers completely forbid all relationships
Liberal believers forbid marriage entirely
Traditional believers require same-sex marriage
questions.explain: Traditional believers tend to limit sex to heterosexual marriage, whereas more liberal believers may accept committed same-sex relationships.

questions.q: A Roman Catholic couple following official Church teaching want to space out having children. Which method should they use?
options: Natural family planning
The contraceptive pill
Condoms
Sterilisation
questions.explain: Official Catholic teaching permits natural family planning but not artificial methods of contraception.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Religious Studies (4RS1) specification; Religious & Ethical Teachings about Relationships
